newsitem.title: BELGIUM: U.S. sales, PPIs spoil the party for Belgian OLOs.
newsitem.headline: U.S. sales, PPIs spoil the party for Belgian OLOs.

text.p: Belgian government bonds (OLOs) and futures took it on the chin on Friday afternoon and some traders said signs in U.S. data of unabated economic strength meant the market would go on reeling for a while.

Elements in U.S. retail and producer price releases US-ECI showing demand was stronger than expected and higher inflation not far away swept front-month OLO futures off their feet. The yield on the 10-year benchmark OLO BE286= swung higher.
"Those figure were not that brilliant...we are very cautious ...we are not seeing many investors at current levels," a trader said, adding yields would rise further in the near term.
One trader said he now saw the benchmark yield rising to 6.20 percent in the near future. It was at 6.05 percent at 1410 GMT, up from 6.03 percent late on Thursday.
"But even that is not a dramatic level," he said. "At about 6.10 we will see buyers back in the market, insurers and such like will be back by then."

More bullish traders noted the benchmark yield was still down from 6.12 percent at the start of the month and said the differences between the cycles in the U.S. and European economies were sufficiently large to justify forecasts for lower yields in a few months' time.

The bearish trader, however, predicted that European economies would increasingly start showing signs of a pick-up. "There is a bigger chance that yields will go up than there is that they will go down," he said.
"We have seen the bottom of the rate cycle," he added.
He expected U.S. interest rates to go up again. "In May or later...I am convinced they will go (up) further."

He said a 50 basis point hike in Fed funds had been priced in. "But if they hesitate and it is later and later, that is bad for prices." Until there was a Fed decision the market would trade in ranges.
